div.head: IV Eg 3
div.ab: Ðæt is þonne, þæt ic wille, þæt ælc mon sy under borge ge binnan burgum ge buton burgum.
Ðæt þonne his, þæt ic wille, þæt ælc mann sy under borge ge binnan burgum ge butan burgum.
Unusquisque habitans in urbe aut rure sub fideiussore constituatur.
Ðæt þonne his þæt ic wille, þæt ælc mann sy under borge ge binnan burgum ge buton burgum.
Nämlich ich will nun, dass jedermann unter Bürgschaft stehe, sowohl innerhalb von Städten, wie ausserhalb von Städten.
Namely, I will now that every man be under surety, both within boroughs and outside boroughs.
My will is, further, that every man be under surety, whether he live within a borough or in the country.
Namely, then, it is my will that every man is to be under surety both within the boroughs and outside the boroughs.

note.seg: ‘Das ist nun was’ Thorpe, Schmid; s. o. 1¹
‘That is now what’ Thorpe, Schmid; see above 1¹

Vgl. Gl Bürgschaft 5a. b.—In folgender Zeile setzt Versio statt ‘ausserhalb der Stadt’ rure, wie II Cn 24 uppon lande in Ggs. zu binnan byrig stellt.—Will der Zusatz anzeigen, dass das Bürgschaftssystem sich zuerst von den Städten aus verbreitete?

Cf. Gl Bürgschaft 5a. b.—In the following line the Versio puts rure instead of ‘outside the town’, just as II Cn 24 contrasts uppon lande with binnan byrig.—Is the addition meant to indicate that the system of surety spread first from the towns?
Lit. ‘both within boroughs and outside.’ The Latin version has in urbe aut rure, cf. II Cn. 24 binnan byrig…up on lande.
